```{python}

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

# import functions 
import functions as fn

```


Load in the data
```{python}

df_com = pd.read_csv("Data/Hormone_time_series_data_interpolated.csv")

num = fn.df_to_numpy(df_com, "Cortisol")

common_t = df_com["NewTime"].iloc[0:72].values

df_meta = pd.read_csv("Data/redcap_controls.csv")

```


# Perform PCA on cortisol time series data

```{python}

pca = PCA(n_components=10)
pca_res = pca.fit(num)


```


# Visualise the PCA results

According to the readme - 'Metadata is recoded by participants over 3 days. Hormone sampling typically started in the morning of day 2 and therefore ends 24hrs later in the morning of day 3'

```{python}


# get wake times
wake_times= fn.to_integer_wake_time(pd.to_datetime(df_meta['night2_final_wake']).dt.time)

```


```{python}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(2,3,figsize=(10, 6), sharey=True, sharex=True)

ax = ax.flatten()

for i in range(6):
    ax[i].plot(pca_res.components_[i,:])
    ax[i].set_title(f"Principal component {i+1}")
    if i >2:
      ax[i].set_xlabel("Time")
      ax[i].set_xticks(np.arange(0, 72+12, 12), ['12', '16', '20', '24', '04', '08','12'])
  

ax[0].set_ylabel("Loading")
ax[3].set_ylabel("Loading")

y = np.random.uniform(-0.2, 0.38, len(wake_times))
ax[0].plot(wake_times/24 +24,y, 'ro', label="Wake time")


```
